D29-DEVICE-FIELD-PARITY.detail: scripts/shells/linux/common/tailscale_common.sh:215-229 (ts_show_devices, row_fmt/print loop) prints only HOSTNAME, DNS NAME, OS, IPV4, IPV6, ONLINE, LAST SEEN, EXIT, CONNECTION -- EXIT is peer.get('ExitNode') only (yes/no). The Windows counterpart scripts/shells/win/win_common/TailscaleCommon.ps1 (already reviewed/approved, SPW-037/038/039 in windows.md) additionally carries Owner (Get-TailscaleDeviceRow:254-260,267, resolved via .User[UserID].LoginName; printed as its own column, TailscaleCommon.ps1:377) and ExitNodeOption as a value distinct from ExitNode (Get-TailscaleDeviceRow:273; Show-TailscaleDevices:383 renders 'in-use' vs 'offered' vs blank). The official-docs spec text supplied for this very task also prints ExitNodeOption as its own field in the given Linux python example ('p.get("ExitNodeOption")', in the 'List all devices with full detail' command entry) -- so the omission is a gap against both the assigned spec's own example and the already-approved Windows implementation, not merely a stylistic difference. linux.md's SPL-118 row lists the Linux device fields explicitly (HostName/DNSName/OS/IPv4/IPv6/Online/ExitNode/connection label -- correctly, no LastSeen/ExitNodeOption/Owner overclaim in the field list itself) but still marks overall status 'aligned' against TailscaleCommon.ps1, which the field list contradicts. Fix: add an 'offers exit node' column (peer.get('ExitNodeOption')) to ts_show_devices, ideally alongside an Owner column resolved from .User[UserID].LoginName (same JSON shape on both platforms), then update SPL-118's field list and, if a corresponding SPW row for this exact gap does not already exist, note it (mirroring the SPW-038/SPW-039 pattern already used for the earlier LastSeen and panel-gating gaps on this same feature).
